The numbers in this article are wrong. The quoted 0.4 miles/minute "maximum" charging rate isn't limited by battery tech, it's limited by the power available to the charger. High-powered charging stations such as Tesla superchargers can charge modern lithium-battery EVs at rates of well over 100 miles/hour.

The issue with fast-charging any kind of battery electric vehicle is that the electric current required to do so is immense. Domestic 240V electricity supplies are generally in the range of 60-100 amps, tops, which gives you an absolute limit of 1-2 miles of charge per minute depending on your vehicle. There's a reason that the Supercharger cables are so damn thick, they have to carry hundreds of amps.
